candidates.text:
A Wired journalist went to interview John McAfee once and described the following encounter:

‘He loads the bullet into the gleaming silver revolver, spins the cylinder.

"This scares you, right?" he says. Then he puts the gun to his head.
My heart rate kicks up; it takes me a second to respond. "Yeah, I'm scared," I admit. "We don't have to do this."
"I know we don't," he says, the muzzle pressed against his temple. And then he pulls the trigger. Nothing happens. He pulls it three more times in rapid succession. There are only five chambers.

"Reholster the gun," I demand.
He keeps his eyes fixed on me and pulls the trigger a fifth time. Still nothing. With the gun still to his head, he starts pulling the trigger incessantly. "I can do this all day long," he says to the sound of the hammer clicking. "I can do this a thousand times. Ten thousand times. Nothing will ever happen. Why? Because you have missed something. You are operating on an assumption about reality that is wrong."’

candidates.text:
Yes. Switzerland has cheese. Congratulations, everyone. We know.

The slightly more interesting fact is that this is Indian cheese that has actually competed against 1000s of cheeses from around the world and won international awards.

@eleftheriaindia, a Mumbai cheesemaker, had a cheese rank #4 in the world at the 2023 World Cheese Awards, competing against 4,500+ cheeses from 43 countries. It has since picked up more international recognition, including Best Indian Cheese at the 2025 World Cheese Awards in Switzerland.

So maybe, just maybe, the point isn’t “India has better cheese than Switzerland.”

The point is: India makes really bloody good cheese.

And if a PM meeting the Swiss President is an opportunity to put an Indian food business w genuine global credentials in front of Switzerland, why wouldn’t you do it?

We are so used to complaining that India doesn’t market itself, doesn’t build brands, doesn’t export enough cultural soft power etc. And then when someone actually puts an Indian product on the diplomatic table, we’re like:

“BUT SWITZERLAND HAS CHEESE 😭”

Please.

Hatred for the government can survive one cheese basket, guys.

candidates.text:
Last week I had a night terror, throwing myself off the bed and bloodying up my back, sides and arms.  

I dreamt that I was on a runaway train and jumped off in a panic.  

I had night terrors years ago but they'd stopped. They were a significant problem in my life as I'd frequently seriously injure myself. I ended up in the hospital once from it. 

I did some research and it seems that they coincide with sleep deprivation. Happening 1-3 hours after sleep onset. 

This makes sense why I had one: I spent five days at 7,000 ft while also missing my bedtime for consecutive days for social events. Going from sea level to altitude creates acute sleep disruption. Full acclimation happens over several weeks. 

People mistakenly think that bad dreams happen in REM but during REM your brain chemically paralyzes your muscular system so you can't act out. 

Night terrors happen during deep slow wave sleep (stage n3) when your muscles aren't paralyzed, putting you at risk of doing something dangerous with your body, like I did.
